situation.problem_text:
Topic: The Attention Mechanism: How Transformers Read

Target audience: University students (computer science or general STEM background)

Section: section_1 — The Intuition: Contextual Awareness

Lecture lines:
Attention is all about selective focus.
Words need context to be understood.
The model tracks relations between words.

Planned animations:
Fade in word 'Context' in color #FFFFFF at center.
Display vector representation of word in color #FF00FF.
Highlight vector interaction with neighboring word vectors.
Show similarity heatmap between word vectors in #00FFFF.
Animate context vector merging into final word representation.

Section: section_2 — The Mechanism: Queries, Keys, and Values

Lecture lines:
We represent words as three vectors.
Queries find, Keys match, Values store.
This is like a library search.

Planned animations:
Fade in Q, K, V matrices in #FFFF00.
Show Query vector mapping to Key space.
Highlight inner product result in #FF0000.
Softmax operation scales scores to [0,1] in #00FF00.
Weight Value vectors by scaled scores to output.

Section: section_3 — Visualizing Attention Scores (Dot-Product)

Lecture lines:
Dot-products measure word relevance.
Softmax converts scores into weights.
High relevance creates a spotlight.

Planned animations:
Fade in two vectors in #FFFFFF.
Rotate vectors to align with each other.
Show projection line representing dot product.
Flash projection value in #FF00FF.
Scale vectors based on dot product magnitude.

Section: section_4 — Multi-Head Attention: Seeing the Whole Picture

Lecture lines:
One spotlight isn't enough context.
Multiple heads see different relations.
They act like a detective team.

Planned animations:
Display three parallel attention heads in #00FFFF.
Run Q, K, V mechanism in each head.
Show head outputs concatenating into single vector.
Linear projection collapses heads to final dimension.

Section: section_5 — Synthesis: The Transformer Core

Lecture lines:
Attention creates context-aware word embeddings.
This enables deep language understanding.
The foundation of modern Transformers.

Planned animations:
Animate Encoder stack fading in #FFFFFF.
Show multi-head attention block highlighted in #FFFF00.
Animate data flow through Transformer layers.

If a storyboard asset reference points to 'none.svg' or is missing, instantiate a representative Manim primitive (e.g., Square for icons, Dot for markers) with appropriate sizing rather than attempting to load a non-existent file.

When calculating coordinates for axes.c2p(), provide explicit scalar expressions or direct lambda outputs rather than referencing internal mobject functions (e.g., curve.function) to prevent inhomogeneous array errors in NumPy.

To prevent visual obstruction, assign concurrent mobjects to distinct grid cells or non-overlapping areas rather than stacking them on the exact same coordinate, even if they appear sequentially.

When displaying multiple distinct primary components in a two-column layout, vertically divide the 6x6 grid into segments (e.g., Rows A-C and Rows D-F) and assign each component to its own segment.

import numpy as np

    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])

        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
